text: Disney Channel is an American pay television channel and the flagship property of Disney Branded Television, a unit of the Disney Entertainment business segment of the Walt Disney Company. Launched on April 18, 1983, as The Disney Channel as a premium channel on top of basic cable, it initially targeted families due to the availability of home television sets at the time. It dropped "The" from its name in 1997, rebranding as Disney Channel, shifting its focus to children and adolescents aged 6–14. The channel broadcasts original first-run children's television series, theatrically released and original television films, and selected third-party programming. As of November 2023, it is available to approximately 70 million pay television households in the United States, down from its peak of 100 million in 2011. Its international footprint, which once included 46 channels in 33 languages, has declined in parts of Europe and most of the Asia-Pacific due to the launch of Disney+ and competition from streaming and social media platforms. The channel launched nationally at 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time on April 18, 1983, under The Disney Channel, with founding president Alan Wagner helping to develop it; it became available in all 50 U.S. states by September 1983 and reached over 611,000 subscribers by December 1983. It debuted its first made-for-cable movie, Tiger Town, in October 1983, earning a CableACE Award, and achieved profitability by January 1985, with 1.75 million subscribers by that time. In September 1990, TCI's Montgomery, Alabama, system became the first to carry it as a basic cable service. Between 1991 and 1996, more cable providers transitioned it from a premium add-on to a basic tier, though Walt Disney Company executives denied plans to convert it into an ad-supported basic service, calling the shift part of a five-year "hybrid" strategy. On April 6, 1997, it officially rebranded as Disney Channel, though it was occasionally marketed as "Disney" from 1997 to 2002. Television films were produced under Disney Channel Premiere Films starting with Tiger Town in 1983, until October 1997, when the label was replaced with "Disney Channel Original Movies" (DCOM), with the first DCOM being Under Wraps, which premiered on October 25, 1997. The most successful DCOM in terms of popularity and accolades is High School Musical 2, which debuted on August 17, 2007, to 17.2 million viewers, setting a longstanding record for the highest-rated television premiere on the channel. Following it, the second-highest-rated DCOM premieres were Wizards of Waverly Place: The Movie, Camp Rock, Descendants 2, Princess Protection Program, Teen Beach Movie, and Jump In!. It previously held the record for the most-watched basic cable program until December 3, 2007, when ESPN surpassed it with an NFL game. The Cheetah Girls franchise was notably successful in merchandise and sales, with its 2003 debut film premiering to over 84 million global viewers and its sequel to 8.1 million American viewers, becoming the most successful film in the series; an 86-date concert tour featuring the group was ranked among the top 10 concert tours of 2006, selling out with 73,500 tickets in three minutes at one point. Disney Channel holds rights to theatrically released feature films, some shared with sister network Freeform, including films from Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures (such as Walt Disney Pictures, Walt Disney Animation Studios, and Pixar), and also features films from Bagdasarian Productions like The Chipmunk Adventure and Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet Frankenstein, though most are not currently owned by Disney. Between programming and ads, the channel features bumpers, with the creator of the four-note mnemonic introduced in 2002 being Alex Lasarenko, identified by the YouTube documentary channel Defunctland in 2022. ESPN's broadcasts of the Little League World Series have included cross-promotions with music-related Disney Channel properties such as High School Musical, the Jonas Brothers, Camp Rock, and Phineas and Ferb. In March 2023, Disney Channel broadcast a live professional sporting event for the first time, airing a youth-oriented alternate broadcast of an NHL game—the Big City Greens Classic—as part of ESPN's coverage, themed around the animated series Big City Greens and visualizing player and puck data with 3D animated players. Disney Jr. is a daily morning program block for preschoolers, succeeding Playhouse Disney, which launched on April 6, 1997, as part of Disney Channel's morning lineup. On May 26, 2010, Disney General Entertainment Content (then Disney-ABC Television Group) announced the expansion of the block into a 24/7 cable and satellite channel that debuted on March 23, 2012. The channel is commercial-free and competes with other preschool-focused channels like Nick Jr. and Universal Kids (formerly PBS Kids Sprout and Sprout). It features programming from Disney Channel's preschool library and films from the Walt Disney Pictures film library. On its launch, Disney Junior took over the channel space previously held by Soapnet, a Disney-owned network for soap operas, due to the decline of that genre and the rise of on-demand and digital viewing. Soapnet ceased operations on December 31, 2013. The Playhouse Disney block on Disney Channel rebranded as Disney Junior on February 14, 2011, and international channels followed; the names were shortened to "Disney Jr." on June 1, 2024, though pronounced the same. Disney-ABC Television Group had planned to launch a Playhouse Disney-branded channel in the U.S. in 2001 but never did, despite launching it internationally. Disney XD, launched on February 13, 2009, as the successor to Toon Disney, targets young audiences aged 6 to 14, including girls, and features action and comedy programming from Disney Channel and the former Jetix block, along with original and syndicated shows. Unlike Disney Channel and Disney Junior, Disney XD operates as an ad-supported service, similar to Toon Disney. The "XD" in its name has no official meaning, despite being associated with a former Disney.com mini-site called Disney Xtreme Digital. Disney Channel Animation, also known as "Disney Channel Animation," is the television animation production studio division of Walt Disney Studios based in Glendale, California, producing original animated programming for the three main Disney-branded television channels. A live-action production studio based in Studio City, Los Angeles, provides original sitcoms and comedy programs primarily for Disney Channel, with many projects co-produced and financed by the Walt Disney Company. Walt Disney EMEA Productions Limited, located in London, England, co-produces original programs in Europe with other companies. Disney Original Documentary is a banner from Disney Branded Television for documentary programs broadcast on Disney Channel and released on Disney+, launched on December 9, 2021. In 2010, Disney Channel All Star Party was released for the Nintendo Wii, a four-player mascot party game with stages resembling board games featuring characters from shows like Sonny with a Chance, Wizards of Waverly Place, and JONAS L.A. Several video games based on the Phineas and Ferb series were released by Disney Interactive Studios, and the Disney Channel website included Flash games with characters from franchises such as Kim Possible and Hannah Montana. In June 2012, the Walt Disney Company announced it would stop advertising or promoting food or beverage products that do not meet strict nutritional guidelines, making Disney Channel the first media company to take such a stance on junk food marketing to children; advertising appears only as underwriter sponsorships during promotional breaks. On July 1, 2012, Disney Channel began providing Descriptive Video Service audio in compliance with the 21st Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act of 2010, offering audio descriptions for the blind in the 25 largest markets and on the five highest-rated cable and satellite channels, including Disney Channel. This is indicated by an on-screen mark and a 2-tone sound repeated three times at the start of episodes of Gravity Falls, Austin & Ally, Good Luck Charlie, and Phineas and Ferb, and on newer episodes of Little Einsteins on Disney Junior (with ABC placing the mark in the bottom-left corner). Disney Channel has a presence in various regions across the Americas, most of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, and Japan, with former channel versions available or used in Australia, New Zealand, Italy, the United Kingdom and Ireland, Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, Turkey, Spain, and Brazil, though most ceased broadcasting in the early 2020s, with content moving to Disney+ or Disney+ Hotstar. On December 14, 2022, Disney ceased distributing programs in Russia in response to the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine. The channel licenses its programming to certain broadcast and cable channels outside the U.S. (including formerly Family Channel in Canada), regardless of whether a localized feed exists. Some critics have disapproved of Disney Channel's marketing strategy led by Anne Sweeney, president from 1996 to 2014, who focused programming on preteen and teenage girls and reduced animated content. In 2002, nearly all Walt-era and pre-1990s programming was removed from the channel, including the late-night "Vault Disney" block, which previously dominated the schedule since 1983. In 2008, Sweeney stated that Disney Channel, through its multi-platform marketing using television and music, would become "the major profit driver" for the Walt Disney Company. The channel has also pulled or re-shot episodes due to content deemed inappropriate for its audience, either for humor or due to real-life events.
